about.title: Santa Ana Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Ana is home to roughly 335,400 people, and much of daily life here happens on property that belongs to someone else: strip-mall parking lots along Bristol Street, storefronts on 1st Street, apartment stairwells, restaurants, and the county buildings that anchor downtown. When a floor is left slick, a walkway is left cracked, or a stairway is left dark, the person who falls often carries the cost while the property owner carries on. California premises liability law asks a fairly direct question: did the owner or operator know about the hazard, or should they have known, and did they fail to fix it or warn about it? That element, called notice, usually decides these cases. It is why photos of the spill, the names of witnesses, and a prompt request for surveillance footage matter so much. We handle premises liability claims for injured Santa Ana residents on a contingency basis, so you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Ana Residents Choose Us After a Fall

items.title: Notice is the whole ballgame
items.desc: In California you generally must show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and did nothing. We can pursue inspection logs, prior complaints and maintenance records that a person on their own rarely obtains.

items.title: Video disappears fast
items.desc: Many Santa Ana stores and complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days. We can send a preservation demand early, before the recording of your fall is gone.

items.title: Deadlines and shared fault
items.desc: You typically have two years to file, but far less if the property belongs to a city, county or other public entity. California's pure comparative fault rule also means a claim can proceed even if you were partly at fault; your recovery is simply reduced by your share.

items.question: I fell at a county building or on a city sidewalk in downtown Santa Ana. Is the process different?
items.answer: Yes, and the timing matters. Claims against a public entity such as the City of Santa Ana or Orange County require a written government claim on a much shorter timeline than the standard two-year deadline for private property. Missing that window can end the claim before it starts, so speaking with an attorney quickly is important.

items.question: The store says I should have been watching where I was walking. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not under California law. The state follows pure comparative fault, which means a jury or adjuster can assign you a percentage of responsibility and reduce your recovery by that amount rather than eliminating it. Whether the hazard was obvious, marked or hidden is a fact question that evidence like photos and video can help settle.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in Santa Ana?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems manageable, because fall injuries often worsen over the following days. Photograph the hazard and the surrounding area, write down what happened while it is fresh, and ask the property manager for an incident report and any surveillance footage. Then reach out to us, and we will review your claim and advise you on next steps.
